overview: The CC Energy & Environment Committee met to discuss various local environmental issues and municipal initiatives. The committee reviewed tree ordinances, light pollution guidelines, potential data center regulations, rodenticide bans, and the ongoing tracking of the city's Climate Action Plan.

items.title: Black Plastic Zero Waste Initiative Update
items.summary: The committee reviewed progress on the Black Plastic Zero Waste initiatives and discussed next steps for community outreach and researching model ordinances.

items.title: Residential Sustainability and Heat Pump Rebates
items.summary: A committee member shared a personal update on installing home heat pumps and solar panels, prompting a brief discussion on navigating Mass Save and utility rebates.

items.title: Local Tree Initiative Updates
items.summary: The committee received updates on the municipal public tree ordinance, the recruitment of a new Tree Warden, Trees Medford's discounted residential tree program, and an upcoming Miyawaki mini-forest planting event.

items.title: Dark Sky Lighting and Light Trespass Concerns
items.summary: Members discussed light trespass issues from residential LED spotlights and agreed to dedicate a future meeting to developing public educational materials and researching model lighting ordinances.

items.title: Environmental Impacts of Data Centers
items.summary: The committee discussed grid capacity demands, noise, and massive heat generation from data centers, resolving to consult city planning officials and research local regulatory frameworks.

items.title: Rodenticide Restrictions and Pest Management
items.summary: The committee reviewed local progress toward banning anticoagulant rodenticides and discussed inviting the director of Save Arlington Wildlife to present at a future meeting.

items.title: Proposed Recreational Additions at Wright's Pond
items.summary: Barry Ingber reported on a proposal to install plastic docks and water slides at Wright's Pond, highlighting concerns over environmental preservation and public opposition.

items.title: Homeowner Tree Insurance Protection Legislation
items.summary: The committee discussed a pending state bill designed to prevent home insurance companies from arbitrarily forcing homeowners to cut down healthy trees.

items.title: Climate Action and Adaptation Plan Tracking
items.summary: Josh Ekhart-Lee updated the committee on efforts to track the city's progress across approximately 150 climate action points, with plans to present a gap analysis in upcoming meetings.
